subject: Packaging concessions, cap/floor smoothing and orderform redlines
messages:
From: Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

Hi Avery / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We did an internal pricing review and attached a first-pass redline to the Pricing Exhibit and Order Form (ACME_PricingRedline_v1.pdf). The key asks from AcmeCloud are:

- Smoothing of the effective caps/floors so that the minimum commit phases in over the first three quarters instead of landing immediately.
- A packaging concession to allow up to 15% of committed usage to be consumed against non-production/test projects (we'd like a whitelist carve-out so dev/test traffic doesn't immediately hit floor/true-up).
- Clarify escalation and true-up cadence (quarterly vs monthly) and whether bandwidth buckets can be reallocated mid-term.

We included simple numbers in the redline (see tab "FloorProposal") that show a phased floor: 30% / 60% / 100% of committed volume in Q1/Q2/Q3 respectively. That should help us get started while protecting your revenue.

Can you review and share a clean orderform + your counter language? Procurement and Legal (cc'd) would like to see any proposed alternative contract language inline.

Attachments: ACME_PricingRedline_v1.pdf, Acme_SOW_v1.xlsx

Best,
Emily Parks
Head of Cloud Procurement
AcmeCloud, Inc.
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

Thanks Emily — appreciate the clear proposal and the phased numbers. Looping in Karthik for legal and orderform edits; Laura is on commercial sequencing for packaging.

Two quick clarifying asks from our side before we mark up:
- Is Acme expecting the whitelist to permanently exclude dev/test usage from commit calculations, or only for a 3–6 month pilot?
- Can you confirm the proposed true-up cadence (your redline references quarterly true-ups but the orderform currently says monthly true-up)?

We'll push a clean copy of the current orderform and a first-pass counter-redline from Legal later today.

Attachment: redwood-orderform-clean.pdf

Regards,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Renewals & Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

On Tue, Aug 17, 2027 at 09:12 AM Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com> wrote:
> We included simple numbers in the redline (see tab "FloorProposal") that show a phased floor: 30% / 60% / 100% of committed volume in Q1/Q2/Q3 respectively.

Thanks Emily — appreciate the context. I'm attaching an annotated legal redline (karthik_redline_changes.docx) but summarize our primary changes and concerns inline below: 

1) Floor phasing: happy to accept a phased minimum but request explicit definitions for "Quarter 1/2/3" and the measurement window. Proposed language: "Quarter 1" shall mean the first full calendar quarter following the Effective Date; floor percentages apply to billed usage during each quarter's measurement period.

2) Whitelist / dev/test carve-out: we can permit a temporary pilot exclusion for non-prod usage capped at 15% for the first two quarters, contingent on (a) Acme providing a named whitelist of projects/environments within 30 days of effective date, and (b) periodic verification (quarterly sampling). Permanent exclusion is not acceptable.

3) True-up cadence: monthly true-ups are standard for our billing; we can offer a compromise of monthly billing with quarterly true-ups for the purpose of minimum-commit reconciliation. This avoids significant forecasting variance on your side while keeping operational billing consistent.

4) Reallocation: allow one reallocation event per 12 months for unused committed units, subject to mutual written agreement; any additional requests may be treated as a contract amendment.

5) Caps (surge protection) — redline clarifies that caps apply to billable throughput but do not limit API throttling protections; suggested clean clause included.

Please confirm acceptance or highlight the areas you want us to soften. If Acme wants longer pilot windows or different phasing percentages, propose the numbers and we can run a quick unit-economics check.

Attachments: karthik_redline_changes.docx

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Lawson <ben.legal@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

Karthik — thanks for the clear breakdown. We can accept the requirement to deliver a named whitelist within 30 days and quarterly verification. However, the phased floor we proposed is important to our finance team: phasing at 30/60/100 over Q1–Q3 reduces cash strain.

Counter-proposal (numbers):
- Committed annual volume: 12,000 units
- Phased floor application: Q1 = 20% (2,400), Q2 = 50% (6,000 cumulative), Q3+ = 100% (12,000).
- Pilot whitelist: 20% allowance for non-prod for first three quarters (we can sign a pilot attestation).

We also asked whether reallocation could be allowed twice in a 12-month period given our seasonal workload spikes — would Redwood consider two reallocations (rather than one) tied to specific blackout windows?

Attachment: floor-phasing.xlsx

If we can land on language today, procurement wants an executed MAP and signature routing to start onboarding next month.

Best,
Emily Parks
Head of Cloud Procurement
AcmeCloud, Inc.
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

Emily — appreciate the fast turnaround. Internal response to your counter-numbers: we can move to a 20/50/100 phasing (your revised numbers) with the following commercial guardrails: 

- Pilot whitelist at 20% for first three quarters is acceptable, conditional on the attestation you mentioned and quarterly verification.
- We can allow two reallocations in a 12-month period (accepted). Any reallocation must be requested >30 days before the affected quarter and confirmed in writing.
- We'll adopt Karthik's proposed billing compromise: monthly billing with quarterly minimum-commit reconciliation.

Next steps: I'll attach a short Mutual Action Plan that reflects timing and milestones (MAP_Acme_20270817.docx). If Acme legal signs off on the final redline, we'll issue a pre-signed orderform for countersignature and route to Contracts for execution.

Can Ben or your legal rep confirm acceptance of the attached final language? If yes, we'll update HubSpot and push to signature.

Attachments: MAP_Acme_20270817.docx

Thanks — excited to get Acme onboarded.
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Renewals & Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Lawson <ben.legal@acmecloud.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Emily Parks <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging concessions + cap/floor smoothing - redline attached

Avery / Karthik — Acme legal has reviewed the revised language. We have one minor redline to section 4.2 (reallocation timing): replace ">30 days before the affected quarter" with "not less than 30 days prior to the start of the quarter in which the change is to take effect." That is non-substantive but aligns with our internal procurement playbook. Otherwise, we accept the 20/50/100 phasing, the two-reallocation allowance, the pilot whitelist at 20% for three quarters (attestation to be provided), and the monthly billing / quarterly reconciliation approach.

Attached is our final signed redline for your contracts team to ingest: ACME_FinalRedline_approved.pdf

Once Redwood publishes the final orderform we will countersign. Please confirm the expected signature turnaround (we typically return countersigned agreements within 48 business hours once the final doc is received).

Regards,
Ben Lawson
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
AcmeCloud, Inc.
